complexity.notes: Correct under the stated ASCII-only constraint, but the trick breaks for the follow-up (arbitrary Unicode input), where a length-prefixed encoding would be required. The decode of the empty list works incidentally: ''.split(delimiter) yields [''] and pop(-1) clears it, though this is subtle and worth a comment.
complexity.summary: Encodes by joining the strings with an emoji delimiter (plus a trailing delimiter) and decodes by splitting on that delimiter and dropping the final empty segment. Since the delimiter is a non-ASCII character and input strings are guaranteed to be ASCII-only, it can never collide with string content.
